**Regulation (EU) No 229/2013**
**of 13 March 2013**
**laying down specific measures for agriculture in favour of the smaller Aegean islands and repealing Council Regulation (EC) No 1405/2006**

**1. Type and Legal Basis**
This is a **Regulation** of the European Parliament and of the Council. It is based on the **Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)**, specifically **Article 42(1)** and **Article 43(2)**. The regulation was adopted following the ordinary legislative procedure, incorporating the opinions of the European Economic and Social Committee and the national parliaments.

**2. Subject Matter and Scope of Application**
The regulation establishes specific measures to mitigate the difficulties caused by the **insularity, small size, and distance from markets** of the **smaller Aegean islands** (defined as all Aegean islands except Crete and Evia).
*   **Territorial Scope:** Applies to all Aegean islands excluding Crete and Evia.
*   **Sectoral Scope:** Covers agriculture, specifically focusing on supply arrangements, local production support, and accompanying state aid.
*   **Applicability:** The regulation applies to the Union's agricultural products listed in **Annex I to the Treaty** (essential for human consumption, processing, or as agricultural inputs).

**3. Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, and Entitlements**
The regulation establishes a **Support Programme** and specific **Supply Arrangements** to ensure the supply of Union products to the islands and preserve local production.

*   **Support Programme (Article 3):**
    *   Greece must establish a support programme at the most appropriate geographical level, submitted to the Commission for approval.
    *   The programme must include specific supply arrangements (Chapter III) and measures to assist local agricultural production (Chapter IV).
    *   It must define a schedule, financing table, and compatibility with other Union policies (e.g., Common Agricultural Policy, rural development).

*   **Specific Supply Arrangements (Chapter III):**
    *   **Eligibility:** Aid is granted only for products of **sound, fair, and marketable quality**.
    *   **Prohibition:** The dispatch or export of these products from the smaller islands is **prohibited** unless the advantage is reimbursed.
    *   **Aid Calculation:** Aid is determined based on the **additional costs** of marketing, insularity, small size, and distance from markets.
    *   **Certificates:** Aid is granted upon presentation of a **non-transferable certificate** issued by the competent authorities. No security is required for application, though a security may be required for export controls.
    *   **Export Controls:** Exports to third countries or dispatch to the rest of the Union are **prohibited** unless the aid is reimbursed.
    *   **Reimbursement:** The economic advantage (aid amount) must be passed on to the end-user (consumer, processor, or farmer).

*   **Measures to Assist Local Production (Chapter IV):**
    *   The programme must include a quantified description of the current situation, strategy, objectives, and measures.
    *   Direct payments must be established in accordance with **Article 2(d) of Council Regulation (EC) No 73/2009**.
    *   The Commission may adopt **delegated acts** to determine aid amounts for marketing and transport outside the region of production.

*   **State Aid (Chapter V):**
    *   The Commission may authorise **State operating aid** under **Article 108(3) TFEU** for specific sectors producing, processing, marketing, or transporting the listed products.
    *   This aid is intended to alleviate specific constraints (insularity, small size, climate, economic dependency) and is **not subject to the prohibition of Article 107 TFEU** regarding State aid, provided it is notified as part of the support programme.

**4. Key Defined Terms**
*   **Smaller Aegean Islands:** Any islands in the Aegean Sea except the islands of Crete and Evia.
*   **Support Programme:** The framework established by Greece comprising specific supply arrangements and measures to assist local agricultural production.
*   **Specific Supply Arrangements:** The mechanism providing aid to supply the smaller islands with Union products, subject to quality checks, certificate issuance, and export controls.
*   **End-User:** The consumer in the case of direct consumption products, the end processor or packager in the case of processing products, or farmers in the case of animal feed or agricultural inputs.
*   **Insularity, Small Size, and Distance from Markets:** The specific geographical and economic constraints imposed on the smaller Aegean islands that justify the specific measures.
*   **Annex I to the Treaty:** The list of Union agricultural products essential for the smaller islands.

**5. Entry-into-Force and Transitional Provisions**
*   **Entry into Force:** The Regulation enters into force on the day following its publication in the *Official Journal of the European Union*.
*   **Amendments:** The Commission may amend the allocation of resources for specific supply arrangements via implementing acts adopted in accordance with the examination procedure.
*   **State Aid Notification:** Aid notified by Greece under Chapter V is deemed to have been notified within the meaning of Article 108(3) TFEU.
*   **Delegation of Powers:** The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission for a period of **five years** starting from **21 March 2013**. The Commission must submit a report on the delegation not later than nine months before the end of the period. The delegation is tacitly extended for identical periods unless opposed by the European Parliament or the Council.
*   **Repeal:** Council Regulation (EC) No 1405/2006 is repealed. References to the repealed Regulation are construed as references to this Regulation.
*   **Reporting:** Greece must submit an annual report on the implementation of the measures by **30 September** each year. The Commission must submit a general report to the European Parliament and the Council by **31 December 2016**, and thereafter every five years.

**Regulation (EU) No 1300/2013** of the European Parliament and of the Council, of 17 December 2013, on the Cohesion Fund and repealing Council Regulation (EC) No 1084/2006.

The Regulation is based on the second paragraph of Article 177 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). The Regulation establishes the Cohesion Fund as a financial instrument to strengthen the economic, social, and territorial cohesion of the Union in the interests of sustainable development. The Cohesion Fund shall support:

*   **Trans-European Networks (TEN-T):** Projects of European added value, specifically for a total amount of EUR 10 billion, in compliance with Union guidelines.
*   **Technical Assistance:** Provision of technical assistance.
*   **Specific Investment Priorities:** Support for investment priorities within the thematic objectives of Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013, including:
    *   Shifting towards a low-carbon economy (renewables, energy efficiency, smart grids).
    *   Climate change adaptation and risk prevention.
    *   Environmental preservation and resource efficiency (waste, water, biodiversity, urban revitalization).
    *   Sustainable transport (multimodal Single European Transport Area, low-carbon transport systems, railway rehabilitation).
    *   Enhancing institutional capacity of public authorities.

**Key Defined Terms:**
*   **Cohesion Fund:** The financial instrument established by this Regulation to strengthen economic, social, and territorial cohesion.

*   **Investment Priorities:** Detailed objectives set out within the thematic objectives of Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013, which the Cohesion Fund is required to contribute to.
*   **Common Output Indicators:** A set of indicators (listed in Annex I) used to assess the aggregated progress at Union level of operational programme implementation.
*   **Greenhouse Gas Emission Allowance Trading:** The scheme for trading allowances established by Directive 2003/87/EC.

*   **Review:** The European Parliament and the Council shall review the Regulation by 31 December 2020 in accordance with Article 177 TFEU.

**Annexes:**

*   **Annex II:** Provides a correlation table between Regulation (EC) No 1084/2006 and Regulation (EU) No 1300/2013.

**COUNCIL REGULATION (EU, EURATOM) No 1311/2013**
**of 2 December 2013**
**laying down the multiannual financial framework for the years 2014–2020**

**Legal Basis**
Based on the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) Article 312, the Treaty establishing the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom) Article 106a, and the proposal from the European Commission, following the consent of the European Parliament and acting in accordance with a special legislative procedure.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application**
This Regulation establishes the multiannual financial framework (MFF) for the Union and the European Atomic Energy Community for the period 2014 to 2020. It applies to all expenditure and revenue of the Union and Euratom, including those resulting from decisions taken unanimously by the Council after consulting the European Parliament under Article 332 TFEU. The framework covers commitment appropriations and payment appropriations, subject to specific technical adjustments and special instruments designed to ensure budgetary flexibility and stability.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, and Entitlements**

**1. Multiannual Financial Framework (Article 1)**
The MFF is set out in the Annex. It establishes annual ceilings for commitments and payment appropriations, which must respect the ceilings set in Council Decision 2007/436/EC regarding own resources.

**2. Mid-term Review/Revision (Article 2)**
By the end of 2016 at the latest, the Commission must present a review of the MFF's functioning, accounting for the economic situation and macroeconomic projections. This review may be accompanied by a legislative proposal for revision. Crucially, preallocated national envelopes shall not be reduced through such a revision.

**3. Compliance with Ceilings (Article 3)**
*   **Commitment and Payment Ceilings:** The European Parliament, the Council, and the Commission must comply with the annual expenditure ceilings set out in the MFF during each budgetary procedure and when implementing the budget for the year concerned.
*   **Flexibility Instruments:** The special instruments provided for in Articles 9 to 15 ensure flexibility. Commitment appropriations may be entered into the budget over and above the relevant MFF ceilings where necessary to utilize resources from the Emergency Aid Reserve, the European Union Solidarity Fund, the Flexibility Instrument, the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund, the Contingency Margin, or specific flexibility measures for youth unemployment and research.
*   **Guarantees:** Guarantees mobilized for loans under Council Regulation (EC) No 332/2002 or Council Regulation (EU) No 407/2010 must be mobilized over and above the MFF ceilings.

**4. Own Resources Ceiling (Article 4)**
For each year covered by the MFF, the total appropriations for payments (after annual adjustment and technical adjustments) must not produce a call-in rate for own resources exceeding the own resources ceiling set in Decision 2007/436/EC. Where necessary, the MFF ceilings may be lowered via revision to ensure compliance.

**5. Global Margin for Payments (Article 5)**
Starting in 2015, the Commission shall adjust the payment ceiling upwards by an amount equivalent to the difference between executed payments and the MFF payment ceiling of the previous year.
*   **Maximum Allowance:** The annual adjustment shall not exceed the following maximum amounts (in 2011 prices) compared to the original payment ceiling:
    *   2018: EUR 7 billion
    *   2019: EUR 9 billion
    *   2020: EUR 10 billion
*   Any upward adjustment must be fully offset by a corresponding reduction of the payment ceiling for the preceding year.

**6. Technical Adjustments (Article 6)**
The Commission shall make technical adjustments to the MFF each year, acting ahead of the budgetary procedure for the following year. These adjustments include:
*   Revaluation of ceilings and appropriations figures at year n+1 prices.
*   Calculation of the margin available under the own-resources ceiling.
*   Calculation of the absolute amount of the Contingency Margin (Article 13) and the Global margin for payments (Article 5) and commitments (Article 14).
*   Calculation of the Global margin for commitments for growth and employment (Article 14).
*   The Commission shall use a fixed deflator of 2% per year for these calculations.
*   No further technical adjustments shall be made for the year concerned, either during the year or as ex-post corrections in subsequent years.

**7. Cohesion Policy Envelopes (Article 7)**
In 2016, the Commission shall review all Member States' total allocations under the "Investment for growth and jobs" goal of cohesion policy for the years 2017–2020.
*   **Method:** Adjustments are applied based on the then-available most recent statistics and a comparison of cumulated national GDP (2014–2015) versus estimated cumulated national GDP (2012).
*   **Threshold:** Adjustments are applied whenever there is a cumulative divergence of more than +/- 5%.
*   **Timing:** Adjustments are spread in equal proportions over the years 2017–2020, and the corresponding MFF ceilings are modified accordingly.
*   **Limit:** The total net effect of these adjustments shall not exceed EUR 4 billion.

**8. Adjustments Related to Economic Governance (Article 8)**
In the event of the lifting of budgetary commitments concerning the European Regional Development Fund, the European Social Fund, the Cohesion Fund, the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development, or the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund due to measures linking effectiveness of funds to sound economic governance, the Commission shall transfer the suspended commitments to subsequent years. Suspended commitments of year n may not be re-budgeted beyond year n+3.

**Special Instruments (Articles 9–16)**
*   **Emergency Aid Reserve (Article 9):** An annual amount of EUR 280 million (2011 prices) intended for rapid response to specific aid requirements of third countries (e.g., humanitarian operations, civil crisis management, migratory flows). It is entered in the general budget as a provision, with the portion from the previous year drawn on first.
*   **European Union Solidarity Fund (Article 10):** A ceiling of EUR 500 million (2011 prices) for financial assistance in major disasters. At least one quarter of the annual amount must remain available until the end of the year.
*   **Flexibility Instrument (Article 11):** A ceiling of EUR 471 million (2011 prices) for financing clearly identified expenditure not covered by other MFF headings. Unused portions may be carried forward up to year n+3.
*   **European Globalisation Adjustment Fund (Article 12):** A maximum annual amount of EUR 150 million (2011 prices).
*   **Contingency Margin (Article 13):** A margin of up to 0.03% of the Union's Gross National Income, constituting a last-resort instrument. It may only be mobilized in relation to an amending or annual budget.
*   **Global Margin for Commitments (Article 14):** Margins left below MFF ceilings for 2014–2017 constitute a Global MFF Margin for 2016–2020, available over and above the MFF ceilings for growth and employment objectives.
*   **Specific Flexibility for Youth Employment (Article 15):** Up to EUR 2,543 million (2011 prices) may be frontloaded in 2014 and 2015 for specified policy objectives (youth employment, research, ERASMUS, SMEs). This amount is fully offset against appropriations within and/or between headings to leave unchanged the total annual ceilings for 2014–2020.
*   **Large-Scale Projects (Article 16):** Maximum amounts available from the general budget for specific projects:
    *   European satellite navigation programmes (EGNOS and Galileo): EUR 6,300 million (2011 prices).
    *   International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER): EUR 2,707 million (2011 prices).
    *   Copernicus (European Earth Observation Programme): EUR 3,786 million (2011 prices).

**Revision Provisions (Articles 17–26)**
*   **Revision (Article 17):** The MFF may be revised in compliance with the own-resources ceiling if unforeseen circumstances arise. Proposals must be presented before the start of the budgetary procedure for the year or the first of the concerned years.
*   **Implementation (Article 18):** The Commission may propose revisions to total payment appropriations based on implementation results. The European Parliament and the Council must decide on these proposals before 1 May of year n.
*   **New Rules/Programmes (Article 19):** If new rules or programmes are adopted after 1 January 2014 for the Structural Funds, Cohesion Fund, etc., the MFF shall be revised to transfer unused allocations from 2014 to subsequent years

**Regulation (EU) No 598/2014**
**of the European Parliament and of the Council**
**of 16 April 2014**
**on the establishment of rules and procedures with regard to the introduction of noise-related operating restrictions at Union airports within a Balanced Approach and repealing Directive 2002/30/EC**

**Legal Basis**
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) Article 100(2).

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application**
This Regulation establishes a harmonised framework for the introduction of noise-related operating restrictions at Union airports located in Member States with more than 50,000 civil aircraft movements per calendar year. It applies to aircraft engaged in civil aviation and excludes military, customs, police, and fire-fighting aircraft, as well as aircraft engaged in exceptional operations (e.g., search and rescue, medical assistance, disaster relief). The Regulation applies to airports where a noise problem has been identified and where the introduction of such restrictions is being considered.

**Primary Obligations and Key Provisions**

**1. Noise Assessment and Balanced Approach**
Member States must assess the noise situation at individual airports in accordance with Directive 2002/49/EC. Where a noise problem is identified, the **Balanced Approach** must be adopted to address noise management. This approach requires a consistent, cost-effective method to address noise problems airport-by-airport, considering measures at the source, land-use planning, operational procedures, and operating restrictions.

**2. Competent Authorities**
Member States must designate independent competent authorities responsible for adopting operating restrictions. These authorities must be independent of any organisation affected by the noise-related action and must notify the Commission of their designations.

**3. Operating Restrictions and Marginally Compliant Aircraft**
*   **Definition:** An "operating restriction" is a noise-related action limiting access to or reducing operational capacity, including the withdrawal of "marginally compliant aircraft."
*   **Marginally Compliant Aircraft:** These are aircraft certified with a cumulative margin of less than 8 EPNdB during a transitional period (ending 14 June 2020) and less than 10 EPNdB thereafter.
*   **Exemptions:**
    *   **Developing Countries:** Marginally compliant aircraft registered in developing countries may be exempted from restrictions to avoid undue economic hardship, provided they meet specific certification, registration, and operational criteria.
    *   **Exceptional Operations:** Authorities may authorise specific operations (e.g., humanitarian aid flights, alterations/repairs) for marginally compliant aircraft that would otherwise be restricted.
*   **Withdrawal Limits:** Following notification, no additional services (beyond the number of movements of marginally compliant aircraft in the previous year) shall be allowed at the airport six months after notification. The annual rate for reducing movements shall not exceed 25% of the total fleet of marginally compliant aircraft.

**4. Cost-Effectiveness and Selection**
Member States must ensure that the noise abatement objective is defined, measures are identified, and their cost-effectiveness is thoroughly evaluated. The preferred measure or combination of measures must be selected without detriment to safety. Measures must be non-discriminatory and necessary to achieve environmental noise abatement objectives.

**5. Consultation and Notification**
*   **Notification:** Before introducing an operating restriction, authorities must provide six months' notice to the Member State, the Commission, and interested parties.
*   **Review:** The Commission may review the process within three months of receiving notice. If the process is not followed, the Commission may notify the competent authority.
*   **Consultation:** Interested parties must be consulted in a transparent manner, with at least three months prior to adoption. This includes local residents, businesses, airport operators, aircraft operators, air navigation service providers, and the Network Manager.
*   **Dispute Resolution:** A mechanism for dispute resolution must be provided.

**6. Data and Information**
*   **Noise Performance Information:** Aircraft operators must communicate noise documentation (including nationality, registration mark, and modifications) to the Commission. The European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) must verify this data for modelling purposes and make it available to competent authorities, aircraft operators, and air navigation service providers.
*   **Central Database:** Data must be stored in a central database and made available for operational purposes.

**Entry into Force and Transitional Provisions**
*   **Entry into Force:** This Regulation shall enter into force on **13 June 2016**.
*   **Repeal:** Directive 2002/30/EC is repealed with effect from **13 June 2016**.
*   **Existing Restrictions:** Noise-related operating restrictions adopted before 13 June 2016 remain in force until revised in accordance with this Regulation.
*   **New Restrictions:** Noise-related operating restrictions adopted after 13 June 2016 may be adopted in accordance with Directive 2002/30/EC if the consultation process was ongoing at that date, provided they are adopted no later than one year after the date of adoption.
*   **Delegation:** The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from **13 June 2016**. The Commission must submit a report on the delegation not later than nine months before the end of the period. The delegation may be tacitly extended for identical periods unless opposed by the European Parliament or the Council.

**INTERINSTITUTIONAL AGREEMENT**
**BETTER LAW-MAKING**
**of 13 April 2016**

**Type and Legal Basis:**
This is an **Interinstitutional Agreement** (specifically, an agreement between the European Parliament, the Council of the European Union, and the European Commission). It is based on **Article 295 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)**.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application:**
The Agreement establishes the principles and mechanisms for **Better Law-Making** within the European Union. Its scope covers the entire legislative cycle, including:
*   **Programming:** Annual and multiannual programming for Union legislation.
*   **Tools:** Impact assessments, public and stakeholder consultation, and ex-post evaluation of existing legislation.
*   **Legislative Instruments:** The use of delegated acts and implementing acts, including the Common Understanding on Delegated Acts.
*   **Transparency and Coordination:** Procedures for information exchange, synchronisation of legislative proposals, and the development of a joint database on legislative files.
*   **Simplification:** Promoting regulatory efficiency, reducing administrative burdens, and using techniques like recasting.

**Primary Obligations and Key Provisions:**

**1. Common Commitments and Objectives (Articles I)**
The three Institutions agree to pursue Better Law-Making through a series of initiatives. Key obligations include:
*   Observing general principles of Union law, including **democratic legitimacy, subsidiarity, proportionality, and legal certainty**.
*   Promoting **simplicity, clarity, and transparency** in the drafting and legislative process.
*   Ensuring Union legislation is **comprehensible and practical** for citizens, administrations, and businesses, particularly SMEs.
*   Prioritising initiatives that offer "European added value" and avoiding the "cost of non-Europe."

**2. Programming and Planning (Articles II)**
*   **Annual Programming:** The Commission engages in a dialogue with the Parliament and Council regarding the Commission Work Programme. This dialogue includes early exchanges on major political initiatives ("letter of intent") and exchanges on the adopted Work Programme.
*   **Joint Declarations:** Following the adoption of the Commission Work Programme, the three Institutions exchange views to agree on a **Joint Declaration on Annual Interinstitutional Programming**, signed by the Presidents. This declaration sets broad objectives and priorities for the following year.
*   **Mid-term Review:** The Commission is required to carry out a mid-term review of these joint conclusions and adjust them as appropriate.

**3. Tools for Better Law-Making (Articles III)**
*   **Impact Assessments:**
    *   Must cover the existence, scale, and consequences of a problem, and whether Union action is needed.
    *   Must map out alternative solutions and assess costs and benefits (economic, environmental, social) using qualitative and quantitative analyses.
    *   Must respect subsidiarity, proportionality, and fundamental rights.
    *   Must address the "cost of non-Europe" and impacts on SMEs, digital aspects, and territorial impact.
    *   The Commission's Regulatory Scrutiny Board conducts an objective quality check.
*   **Public and Stakeholder Consultation:**
    *   The Commission must conduct public consultations in an open and transparent manner before adopting proposals, encouraging direct participation by SMEs and end-users.
    *   Results must be communicated without delay to both co-legislators and made public.
*   **Ex-post Evaluation:**
    *   The Commission must inform Parliament and Council of its multiannual planning for evaluations of existing legislation.
    *   Evaluations should provide the basis for impact assessments of further action options.
    *   The three Institutions agree to systematically consider the use of **review clauses** (sunset clauses) in legislation to limit application to a fixed period.

**4. Legislative Instruments (Articles IV and V)**
*   **Explanatory Memoranda:** The Commission must provide an explanation and justification for the choice of legal basis and type of legal act to the Parliament and Council.
*   **Delegated and Implementing Acts:**
    *   The Commission must gather all necessary expertise (including Member States' experts) prior to adopting delegated acts.
    *   The Commission must ensure **simultaneous transmission** of all documents to the Parliament, Council, and Member States' experts.
    *   **Time Limits for Objection:** The period for expressing objections to a delegated act is generally **two months** (extendable by two months at the initiative of the Parliament or Council).
    *   **Urgency Procedure:** Reserved for exceptional cases (security, health, external relations). If adopted under this procedure, the act enters into force without delay and applies until an objection is raised.
    *   **Common Understanding:** The Agreement establishes a Common Understanding on Delegated Acts (Annex), which sets out standard clauses for consultations, document transmission, and time periods.

**5. Transparency and Coordination (Articles VI)**
*   The three Institutions agree to maintain close contacts throughout the legislative process to ensure mutual understanding.
*   They agree to coordinate efforts to accelerate the legislative process while respecting the prerogatives of the co-legislators.
*   They commit to identifying ways to develop platforms and tools for traceability by **31 December 2016**, with a view to establishing a dedicated joint database on the state of play of legislative files.
*   They commit to negotiating improved practical arrangements for cooperation and information-sharing within the framework of the Treaties within **six months** after the entry into force of this Agreement.

**6. Implementation and Monitoring (Article IX)**
*   The three Institutions will monitor the implementation of this Agreement jointly, both at the political level (annual discussions) and the technical level (Interinstitutional Coordination Group).

**7. Final Provisions (Article X)**
*   This Agreement replaces the Interinstitutional Agreement on Better Law-Making of 16 December 2003 and the Interinstitutional Common Approach to Impact Assessment of November 2005.
*   It enters into force on the day of its signature.
*   The text is available in multiple official languages.

**Entry-into-Force Date:**
The Agreement enters into force on the day of its signature.

**DIRECTIVE (EU) 2017/1371 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL**
**of 5 July 2017**
**on the fight against fraud to the Union's financial interests by means of criminal law**

**Legal Basis:**
The Directive is based on **Article 83(2) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)** and the **Convention on the protection of the European Communities' financial interests** (1995), including its Protocols. It was adopted following the ordinary legislative procedure, incorporating the opinions of the Committee of the Regions and the European Court of Auditors.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application**
The Directive establishes minimum rules concerning the definition of criminal offences and sanctions to combat fraud and other illegal activities affecting the Union's financial interests. It applies to:
*   **Union's financial interests:** Revenues, expenditure, and assets covered by the Union budget, the budgets of Union institutions, bodies, offices, and agencies (including those directly or indirectly managed and monitored by them), and revenues arising from VAT own resources.
*   **Territorial Scope:** The Directive applies to fraud committed within the territory of two or more Member States, involving a total damage of at least EUR 10,000,000, or involving cross-border fraudulent schemes regarding VAT own resources. It also applies to fraud committed using information and communication technology accessed from the territory of a Member State.
*   **Legal Persons:** Legal persons are liable for criminal offences committed on their behalf if they have a power of representation, authority to take decisions, or authority to exercise control.
*   **Exclusions:** The Directive does not oblige Member States to provide for imprisonment for non-serious offences where intent is presumed under national law. It does not affect the application of disciplinary measures or other non-criminal penalties.

**Primary Obligations and Key Provisions**

**1. Definition of Fraud (Article 3)**
Member States must ensure that the following constitute criminal offences:
*   **Non-procurement fraud:** Misappropriation or wrongful retention of funds/assets via false statements/documents, non-disclosure of information, or misapplication of funds.
*   **Procurement fraud:** Unlawful gains for the perpetrator or others, involving false statements, non-disclosure, or misapplication of funds.
*   **Revenue fraud (non-VAT):** Illegal diminution of Union budget resources via false statements, non-disclosure, or misapplication of benefits.
*   **Revenue fraud (VAT own resources):** Cross-border schemes involving false VAT statements, non-disclosure of VAT information, or fraudulent disguising of non-payment/rights to refunds.

**2. Definition of Corruption (Article 4)**
*   **Passive corruption:** The action of a public official (including contractors assigned to manage Union funds) who requests or receives advantages to act or refrain from acting in accordance with their duty, damaging Union financial interests.
*   **Active corruption:** The action of a person who promises, offers, or gives an advantage to a public official to act or refrain from acting in accordance with their duty, damaging Union financial interests.

**3. Definition of Misappropriation (Article 4)**
The action of a public official entrusted with the management of funds/assets who commits or disbursements assets contrary to their intended purpose, damaging Union financial interests.

**4. Liability of Legal Persons (Article 6)**
Legal persons can be held liable for offences committed for their benefit if they exercise representation, decision-making, or control powers. Liability does not exclude criminal proceedings against natural persons.

**5. Sanctions for Natural Persons (Article 7)**
*   **Imprisonment:** Mandatory imprisonment is required for offences involving considerable damage or advantage.
*   **Thresholds:**
    *   For offences involving considerable damage/advantage: Presumed to be considerable if the damage/advantage exceeds **EUR 100,000**.
    *   For VAT own resources offences: Always presumed to be considerable if the damage/advantage exceeds **EUR 10,000,000**.
*   **Other Serious Circumstances:** Member States may provide for imprisonment up to four years in other serious circumstances defined by national law.

**DECISION (EU) 2018/646 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL**
**of 18 April 2018**
**on a common framework for the provision of better services for skills and qualifications (Europass) and repealing Decision No 2241/2004/EC**

**Legal Basis:**
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) Articles 165 and 166.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application**
This Decision establishes a European framework to support the transparency and understanding of skills and qualifications acquired in formal, non-formal, and informal settings, including through practical experiences, mobility, and volunteering. The framework, referred to as **Europass**, consists of web-based tools and relevant information, including an online platform and national services, intended to help users better communicate, present, and compare skills and qualifications.

The framework is targeted at:
*   **Individual end-users:** Learners, job seekers, workers, volunteers, and unemployed persons.
*   **Relevant stakeholders:** Education and training providers, guidance practitioners, employers, public employment services, social partners, youth work providers, youth organisations, and policy makers.

The use of Europass is **voluntary** and does not impose any obligations or confer rights other than those defined herein.

**Primary Obligations and Entitlements**
The core obligations and entitlements established by this Decision are as follows:

1.  **Framework Composition:** Europass shall consist of web-based tools and relevant information, including an online platform and national services, to facilitate the description and comparison of skills and qualifications.
2.  **Targeting:** The framework must be accessible to persons with disabilities in accordance with relevant Union law and ensure technical interoperability and synergies with other Union instruments.
3.  **Open Standards and Free Access:** Web-based tools shall use open standards to be made available free of charge for reuse by Member States and other stakeholders.
4.  **Language and Accessibility:** Tools shall be delivered in the official languages of the Union and must be perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust to ensure equal access for persons with disabilities.
5.  **Data Protection:** The processing of personal data stored and processed pursuant to this Decision must comply with Union law on the protection of personal data (specifically Directive 95/46/EC and Regulation (EC) No 45/2001). Users must have the possibility to restrict access to their personal data.
6.  **Transparency and Validation:** The framework shall support the validation of non-formal and informal learning, ensuring that individuals can obtain full or partial qualifications where applicable.
7.  **Transitional Arrangements:** The existing Europass internet-based information system established by Decision No 2241/2004/EC shall continue to operate until the new Europass online platform is set up and becomes operational.

**Key Defined Terms**
*   **Certificate supplement:** A document attached to a vocational education and training or professional certificate to facilitate understanding of learning outcomes, nature, level, context, content, and status of the education and training completed.
*   **Diploma supplement:** A document attached to a higher education diploma to facilitate understanding of learning outcomes, nature, level, context, content, and status of the education and training completed.
*   **Europass supplements:** A set of documents (e.g., diploma and certificate supplements) issued by competent authorities or bodies.
*   **Guidance:** A continuous process enabling individuals to identify their capacities, skills, and interests through individual and collective activities to make educational, training, and occupational decisions and manage their life paths.
*   **European dimension of guidance:** Cooperation and support at Union level to strengthen policies, systems, and practices for guidance within the Union.
*   **Qualification:** A formal outcome of an assessment and validation process obtained when a competent authority or body determines that an individual has achieved learning outcomes to given standards.
*   **Skills intelligence:** Available quantitative or qualitative analysis of aggregated data on skills from existing sources in relation to the labour market and corresponding learning opportunities in the education and training system.
*   **Self-assessment of skills:** The process of systematic reflection by individuals on their skills through reference to an established description of skills.
*   **Skills:** In the context of this Decision, skills are understood in a broad sense covering what a person knows, understands, and can do, including knowledge, competences, and the ability to apply knowledge and knowhow to complete tasks and solve problems.
*   **Technical interoperability:** The ability of information and communication technology systems to interact so as to enable the sharing of information, achieved through agreement by all parties and owners of the information.
*   **Validation:** The process by which a competent authority or body confirms that an individual has acquired learning outcomes, including those acquired in non-formal and informal learning settings, measured against a relevant standard, consisting of four distinct phases: identification, documentation, assessment, and certification of results (full qualification, credits, or partial qualification).
*   **Open standards:** Technical standards developed in a collaborative process and published for free use by any interested party.
*   **Online platform:** A web-based application providing information and tools to end users to complete specific tasks online.
*   **Personal data:** Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.

**Entry-into-Force and Transitional Provisions**
*   **Entry into force:** This Decision shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the *Official Journal of the European Union*.
*   **Transitional provisions:**
    *   Decision No 2241/2004/EC is repealed.
    *   The Europass internet-based information system established by Decision No 2241/2004/EC shall continue to operate until the Europass online platform established by this Decision is set up and becomes operational.

**Financial Provisions**
The implementation of this Decision at national level shall be co-financed through Union programmes. The annual appropriations shall be authorised by the European Parliament and the Council within the limits of the multiannual financial framework.

**Co-funding**
Co-funding for the implementation of this Decision is provided, inter alia, by the Union programme **Erasmus+**, established by Regulation (EU) No 1288/2013.

**Advisory Group**
The Commission shall ensure the coherent implementation and monitoring of this Decision through a Europass advisory group composed of representatives of the Member States and relevant stakeholders. This group shall develop a strategic approach to the implementation and future development of Europass, advise on the development of web-based tools, and provide information on the Europass online platform.

**Participation**
Participation in the activities referred to in this Decision shall be open to:
1.  Members of the European Economic Area which are not Member States of the Union, in accordance with the conditions laid down in the Agreement on the European Economic Area.
2.  Acceding States, candidate States, and potential candidate States for accession to the Union, in accordance with their agreements concluded with the Union.

**Repeal**
Decision No 2241/2004/EC is repealed, without prejudice to the validity or status of previously issued Europass documents. All established Europass document templates shall be maintained within the new framework until such time as necessary changes or updates are made in accordance with this Decision.

**Directive (EU) 2018/958 of the European Parliament and of the Council**
**of 28 June 2018**
**on a proportionality test before adoption of new regulation of professions**

**Legal Basis:**
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) Articles 46, 53(1), and 62; Directive 2005/36/EC.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application:**
This Directive establishes a common framework for proportionality assessments conducted by Member States prior to the introduction of new or the amendment of existing legislative, regulatory, or administrative provisions restricting access to, or the pursuit of, regulated professions. It applies to requirements limiting access to or the pursuit of existing regulated professions or new professions under Directive 2005/36/EC, as well as new professions being considered for regulation. It does not apply where specific requirements are established in a separate Union act that leaves Member States no choice regarding the method of transposition.

**Primary Obligations and Prohibitions:**
Member States are required to conduct an *ex ante* assessment of proportionality before adopting new measures. This assessment must be:
*   **Objective and Independent:** Carried out by authorities independent of the profession being regulated, potentially involving independent bodies or local authorities where necessary to identify risks.
*   **Evidence-Based:** Justification for regulation must be accompanied by an analysis of appropriateness and proportionality supported by qualitative and quantitative elements.
*   **Non-Discriminatory:** Provisions must not discriminate on grounds of nationality or residence.
*   **Justified by Public Interest:** Measures must be justified by public interest objectives such as public policy, public security, public health, consumer protection, the administration of justice, fair trade, combating fraud, transport safety, environmental protection, animal health, intellectual property, heritage, social policy, and cultural policy.
*   **Proportionate:** Measures must be suitable for attaining the objective and not go beyond what is necessary. This includes considering alternative, less restrictive means (e.g., protected professional titles or enrolment on registers) where risks are limited to the professional-consumer relationship.
*   **Comprehensive:** Assessments must consider the combined effect of new provisions with other existing requirements (e.g., mandatory membership, ethics, supervision, insurance, tariffs, advertising).

**Key Defined Terms:**
*   **Protected professional title:** A form of regulation where the use of a title is subject to possession of a specific professional qualification and sanctions for improper use.
*   **Reserved activities:** A form of regulation where access to a professional activity is reserved to members of a regulated profession holding a specific qualification.
*   **Overriding reasons in the public interest:** Specific reasons recognized by the Court of Justice, including preserving the financial equilibrium of the social security system, protecting consumers and workers, safeguarding the administration of justice, ensuring fair trade, combating fraud, safeguarding fiscal supervision, transport safety, environmental protection, animal health, intellectual property, heritage, social policy, and cultural policy.
*   **Asymmetry of information:** The situation where professionals possess high technical knowledge that consumers may not have, potentially affecting the ability to make informed choices.

**Entry-into-Force and Transitional Provisions:**
*   **Entry into Force:** The Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
*   **Transposition Deadline:** Member States must bring into force the necessary laws, regulations, and administrative provisions by **30 July 2020**.
*   **Reporting:** The Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and the Council by **18 January 2024**, and every five years thereafter, on the implementation and performance of the Directive.
*   **Information Exchange:** Member States must inform the Commission of the public authorities responsible for transmitting and receiving information regarding the application of the Directive.
*   **Database:** The reasons for considering provisions justified and proportionate must be recorded in the database of regulated professions and made publicly available by the Commission.

**DIRECTIVE (EU) 2018/1673 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL**
**of 23 October 2018**
**on combating money laundering by criminal law**

**Legal Basis:**
The Directive is based on the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), specifically Article 83(1), following the proposal from the European Commission and after transmission to national parliaments. It was adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application**
This Directive establishes minimum rules concerning the definition of criminal offences and sanctions in the area of money laundering. It aims to combat money laundering by criminal law, enabling more efficient and swifter cross-border cooperation between competent authorities.

The Directive applies to all Member States. It explicitly excludes money laundering involving property derived from criminal offences affecting the Union's financial interests, which is governed by Directive (EU) 2017/1371.

**Key Obligations and Provisions**

1.  **Definition of Criminal Activity:**
    Member States must ensure that specific categories of conduct are considered "criminal activity" for the purposes of money laundering. These include:
    *   Participation in organised criminal groups, racketeering, and terrorism.
    *   Trafficking in human beings, migrant smuggling, and sexual exploitation.
    *   Illicit drug trafficking, arms trafficking, and counterfeiting of currency.
    *   Environmental crimes, corruption, fraud, and cybercrime.
    *   Tax crimes relating to direct and indirect taxes.
    *   Extortion, forgery, piracy, and insider trading.
    *   *Note:* Member States may include additional offences within these categories if they are punishable by imprisonment for a minimum of six months.

2.  **Criminalisation of Money Laundering:**
    Member States must criminalise the following conduct when committed intentionally with knowledge that the property was derived from criminal activity:
    *   Conversion or transfer of property to conceal or disguise its illicit origin.
    *   Concealment or disguise of the true nature, source, location, disposition, movement, rights, or ownership of property.
    *   Acquisition, possession, or use of property knowing it was derived from criminal activity.
    *   *Optional:* Member States may also criminalise conduct where the offender suspected or ought to have known the property was derived from criminal activity.

3.  **Procedural Requirements:**
    *   **No Prior Conviction Requirement:** A prior or simultaneous conviction for the underlying criminal activity is not a prerequisite for a money laundering conviction.
    *   **No Factual Elements Requirement:** A conviction is possible where it is established that the property was derived from criminal activity, without needing to prove all factual elements or the identity of the perpetrator.
    *   **Territorial Extensibility:** Offences extend to property derived from conduct committed on the territory of another Member State or a third country, provided that conduct would constitute a criminal activity domestically.
    *   **Self-Laundering:** Member States may criminalise money laundering committed by the perpetrator of the underlying criminal activity (e.g., if the property is transferred, converted, concealed, or disguised, resulting in further damage).

4.  **Penalties for Natural Persons:**
    *   Offences must be punishable by effective, proportionate, and dissuasive criminal penalties.
    *   A maximum term of imprisonment of at least **four years** is mandatory.
    *   Additional sanctions may be imposed, such as fines, exclusion from public funding, disqualification from commercial activities, bans on running for office, or judicial supervision.
    *   Judges and courts may consider aggravating circumstances (e.g., involvement in a criminal organisation, being an obliged entity, or dealing with high-value property) when sentencing.

5.  **Liability of Legal Persons:**
    *   Legal persons can be held liable for offences committed for their benefit by individuals acting in their name or on their behalf (e.g., via power of representation, decision-making authority, or control).
    *   Liability may also arise where a lack of supervision or control by a responsible person facilitated the offence.
    *   Criminal proceedings against natural persons (perpetrators, inciters, accessories) are not precluded by liability of legal persons.

6.  **Confiscation:**
    Member States must ensure that competent authorities freeze or confiscate proceeds and instrumentalities used in the commission of the offences, in accordance with Directive 2014/42/EU.

7.  **Jurisdiction:**
    *   Each Member State must establish jurisdiction over offences committed on its territory or by its nationals.
    *   Member States may extend jurisdiction to habitual residents or offences benefiting a legal person established on their territory.
    *   In cases of concurrent jurisdiction, Member States must cooperate to centralise proceedings in a single Member State, taking into account factors such as the territory of the offence, the offender's nationality, the victim's origin, and the offender's location.

8.  **Investigative Tools:**
    Persons responsible for investigating or prosecuting money laundering offences must have access to effective investigative tools used in combating organised crime or other serious crimes, including sufficient personnel, training, and technological capacity.

9.  **Aggravating Circumstances:**
    Member States may consider the following as aggravating circumstances:
    *   Commitment within a criminal organisation (per Framework Decision 2008/841/JHA).
    *   Commitment by an obliged entity in the exercise of professional activities (per Directive 2015/849).
    *   Laundered property of considerable value.
    *   Laundered property deriving from specific categories of offences listed in Article 2(1)(a) to (e) and (h).

10. **Replacement of Framework Decision 2001/500/JHA:**
    This Directive replaces certain provisions of Council Framework Decision 2001/500/JHA for Member States bound by it, without prejudice to the transposition deadline for that Framework Decision.

**Key Defined Terms**
*   **Criminal Activity:** Any kind of criminal involvement in the commission of any offence punishable by deprivation of liberty or detention for a maximum of more than one year, or by deprivation of liberty/detention for a minimum of more than six months.
*   **Property:** Assets of any kind (corporeal or incorporeal, movable or immovable, tangible or intangible), including legal documents or instruments evidencing title or interest in such assets.
*   **Legal Person:** Any entity having legal personality under applicable law, excluding states or public bodies in the exercise of state authority and public international organisations.

**Entry into Force and Transitional Provisions**
*   **Entry into Force:** This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
*   **Transposition Deadline:** Member States must bring into force the necessary laws, regulations, and administrative provisions by **3 December 2020**.
*   **Reporting:**
    *   The Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and the Council by **3 December 2022** assessing compliance.
    *   The Commission shall submit a report by **3 December 2023** assessing the added value and impact on fundamental rights.
    *   Based on the 2023 report, the Commission may present a legislative proposal to amend the Directive if necessary.
*   **Addressees:** This Directive is addressed to the Member States.
*   **Exclusion:** The United Kingdom and Ireland are not taking part in the adoption or are not bound by this Directive. Denmark is not taking part but remains bound by Council Framework Decision 2001/500/JHA.

**Regulation (EU) 2018/643 of the European Parliament and of the Council**
**of 18 April 2018**
**on rail transport statistics (recast)**

**Legal Basis**
Based on Article 338(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and following the proposal from the European Commission, after consultation of the European Economic and Social Committee, and acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application**
This Regulation establishes common rules for the production of rail transport statistics at Union level. It covers all railways within the European Union. Each Member State is required to report statistics relating to rail transport on its national territory. The scope includes:
*   **Railway Undertakings:** Public or private undertakings providing services for the transport of goods and/or passengers by rail.
*   **Exclusions:** The Regulation explicitly excludes railway undertakings that operate entirely or mainly within industrial installations (including harbours) and those that mainly provide local tourist services (e.g., preserved historical steam railways).
*   **Excluded Transport Modes:** Metro, tram, and light rail transport are excluded from the definition of "rail transport" for the purposes of this Regulation.

**Primary Obligations and Entitlements**
The core obligation is for Member States to collect and report specific statistical data on goods and passenger transport, as well as traffic flows, to Eurostat.
*   **Data Collection Thresholds:** Member States must report data for undertakings meeting specific volume thresholds:
    *   For goods transport: A total volume of at least 200 million tonne-km or 500 million tonnes.
    *   For passenger transport: A total volume of at least 100 million passenger-km.
    *   Undertakings falling below these thresholds are not required to report under Annexes I and II but must report total data under Annex VIII.
*   **Reporting Frequency and Periodicity:**
    *   **Annual Statistics (Annexes I, II, VIII):** Reported every year.
    *   **Quarterly Statistics (Annex III):** Reported every quarter.
    *   **Regional Statistics (Annex IV):** Reported every five years.
    *   **Traffic Flow Statistics (Annex V):** Reported every five years.
*   **Data Sources:** Member States must designate a public or private organisation to participate in data collection. Data may be obtained from compulsory surveys, administrative data (e.g., freight waybills), statistical estimation procedures, professional industry data, or ad hoc studies.
*   **Quality Assurance:** Eurostat is empowered to develop and publish methodological recommendations to assist Member States in maintaining data quality. Member States must ensure the quality of transmitted data, and Eurostat evaluates the quality of statistical data.
*   **Dissemination:** Statistics based on the data specified in Annexes I to V and VIII shall be disseminated by the Commission (Eurostat).

**Key Defined Terms**
The following terms govern the interpretation of the Regulation:
*   **Reporting Country:** The Member State transmitting data to Eurostat.
*   **Railway:** A line of communication made up by rail exclusively for the use of railway vehicles.
*   **Railway Vehicle:** Mobile equipment running exclusively on rails, moving either under its own power (tractive vehicles) or hauled by another vehicle (coaches, railcar trailers, vans and wagons).
*   **Railway Undertaking:** Any public or private undertaking providing services for the transport of goods and/or passengers by rail. Metro, tram, and light rail undertakings are excluded.
*   **Transport of Goods by Rail:** The movement of goods using railway vehicles between the place of loading and the place of unloading.
*   **Transport of Passengers by Rail:** The movement of passengers using railway vehicles between the place of embarkation and the place of disembarkation. Metro, tram, and light rail are excluded.
*   **Metro:** An electric railway for the transport of passengers with high capacity, exclusive rights-of-way, multi-car trains, high speed, sophisticated signalling, and no level crossings.
*   **Train:** One or more railway vehicles hauled by one or more locomotives or railcars, running under a given number or specific designation from an initial fixed point to a terminal fixed point. A light engine (locomotive travelling alone) is not considered a train.
*   **Train-Km:** The unit of measure representing the movement of a train over one kilometre.
*   **Full Train Load:** A consignment comprising one or more wagonloads transported at the same time by the same sender at the same station and forwarded with no change in train composition to the address of the same consignee at the same destination station.
*   **Full Wagon Load:** A consignment of goods for which the exclusive use of a wagon is required.
*   **TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit):** A standard unit based on an ISO container of 20 feet length (6.10 m). One standard 40' ISO Series 1 container equals 2 TEUs.
*   **Number of Passengers:** The number of trips by rail passengers, where each trip is defined as the movement from the place of embarkation to the place of disembarkation, with or without transfers.
*   **Passenger-Km:** The unit of measure representing the transport of one passenger by rail over a distance of one kilometre.
*   **Tonne-Km:** The unit of measure of goods transport representing the transport of one tonne of goods by rail over a distance of one kilometre.
*   **National Transport:** Rail transport between two places located in the reporting country, which may involve transit through a second country.
*   **International Transport:** Rail transport between a place in the reporting country and a place in another country.
*   **Transit:** Rail transport through the reporting country between two places outside the reporting country. Operations involving loading/embarkation or unloading/disembarkation at the border from/onto another mode of transport are not considered transit.
*   **Goods Transport:** Classified according to Annex VI.
*   **Dangerous Goods:** Classified according to Annex VII.
*   **NUTS 2:** The standard statistical area for regional statistics.
*   **TEN:** The rail trans-European network.

**Entry-Into-Force and Transitional Provisions**
*   **Entry into Force:** This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the *Official Journal of the European Union*.
*   **Delegation of Powers:** The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 13 December 2016. The Commission must draw up a report not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. The delegation is tacitly extended for identical periods unless the European Parliament or the Council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period.
*   **Repeal:** Regulation (EC) No 91/2003 is repealed. References to the repealed Regulation shall be construed as references to this Regulation and shall be read in accordance with the correlation table in Annex X.

**Regulation (EU) 2018/956 of the European Parliament and of the Council**

**Type and Legal Basis:**
This is a **Regulation** adopted by the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union. It is based on **Article 192(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)**. The regulation was adopted following the ordinary legislative procedure, having received the opinions of the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions.

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application:**
The Regulation establishes a mandatory monitoring and reporting framework for **CO2 emissions and fuel consumption** from new heavy-duty vehicles (HDVs) registered in the Union. It applies to:
*   **Vehicle Categories:** Vehicles of categories **M1, M2, N1, N2** (with a reference mass exceeding 2,610 kg and not covered by Regulation (EC) No 715/2007), and categories **M3, N3**, as well as categories **O3 and O4**.
*   **Applicability:** The regulation applies to the monitoring and reporting by **Member States** and **manufacturers** of new heavy-duty vehicles.
*   **Exclusions:** Data relating to vehicles registered outside the Union prior to their registration in the Union (unless registered less than three months prior) is not monitored or reported.

**Primary Obligations and Key Provisions:**

**1. Monitoring and Reporting by Member States (Article 4):**
*   Starting from **1 January 2019**, Member States must monitor data specified in **Part A of Annex I** for new heavy-duty vehicles registered in the Union.
*   By **28 February** each year (starting in 2020), competent authorities must report these data to the Commission in accordance with the reporting procedure in **Annex II**.
*   Manufacturers must monitor data specified in **Part B of Annex I** for each new heavy-duty vehicle.
*   Reporting deadlines for manufacturers are by **28 February** each year for vehicles with a simulation date falling in the preceding calendar year.

**2. Monitoring and Reporting by Manufacturers (Article 5):**
*   Manufacturers must monitor and report data specified in **Part B of Annex I** on a calendar year basis.
*   A **contact point** must be appointed by each manufacturer for reporting purposes.
*   The **date of simulation** is defined as the date reported in data entry 71 of Part B of Annex I.

**3. Central Register (Article 6):**
*   The **European Environment Agency (EEA)** shall keep a **Central Register** for data reported under Articles 4 and 5.
*   The Register is publicly available, with specific data entries (e.g., vehicle identification numbers, engine certification numbers, etc.) excluded from public access.
*   Data entry 23 (CdxA value) must be made available in a **range format**.

**4. Verification and Data Quality (Article 8):**
*   Competent authorities and manufacturers are responsible for the correctness and quality of reported data.
*   The Commission shall verify data quality and correct errors where appropriate.
*   The Commission may adopt **implementing acts** to determine verification and correction measures, following an examination procedure.

**5. Administrative Fines (Article 9):**
*   The Commission may impose administrative fines in the following cases:
    *   (a) Where reported data deviate from manufacturer records or engine type-approval certificates (intentional or due to serious negligence), with a maximum fine of **EUR 30,000** per vehicle.
    *   (b) Where data are not submitted within the applicable deadline and the delay cannot be duly justified.
*   The Commission shall adopt **delegated acts** to specify the procedure, calculation methods, and collection criteria for these fines.

**6. Annual Report (Article 10):**
*   The Commission shall publish an **annual report** by **31 October** each year analyzing the data transmitted by Member States and manufacturers.
*   The report must indicate the performance of the Union fleet and each Member State/manufacturer in terms of average fuel consumption and CO2 emissions for each heavy-duty vehicle group by mission profile, load, and fuel combination.

**7. Delegation of Powers (Article 13):**
*   The power to adopt **delegated acts** is conferred on the Commission for a period of **seven years** (starting 29 July 2018).
*   The Commission must submit a report on the delegation not later than nine months before the end of the seven-year period.
*   The delegation may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or the Council.
*   Delegated acts enter into force only if no objection is raised within two months of notification, or if both the Parliament and Council inform the Commission they will not object.

**Key Defined Terms:**
*   **Heavy-duty vehicles:** Defined in Article 2 as vehicles of categories M1, M2, N1, N2 (with reference mass > 2,610 kg and not covered by Regulation (EC) No 715/2007), and categories M3, N3, and O3, O4.
*   **CdxA:** Refers to the **air drag value** (measured in m²), which is a key parameter for determining CO2 emissions and fuel consumption.
*   **WHTC (World Harmonized Transient Driving Cycle):** A test cycle used for calculating engine CO2 emissions.
*   **WHSC (Worldwide Harmonised Steady-state Cycle):** A test cycle used for calculating engine fuel consumption.
*   **EMS (European Modular System):** A standard for road vehicle dimensions and weights within the EU.
*   **SMT, AMT, APT:** Types of transmissions (Synchronised Manual, Automated Manual, Automatic Powershifting).
*   **RRC (Specific rolling resistance coefficient):** A parameter used to calculate fuel consumption.

**Entry into Force and Transitional Provisions:**
